input.quote: each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim
input.rationale:
Section 21 is the only liability regime in the agreement (no competing cap or one-sided "not liable" language elsewhere), and it is structurally strong: the cap is expressly mutual ("each Party's ... The cap is mutual"), § 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually, and the § 21.3 "Excluded Claims" definition already carries every preferred carve-out uncapped — confidentiality, data-protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP — plus the statement that Customer's payment obligation is not damages. Indemnities under § 20 are therefore not swallowed by the cap.

The cap quantum, however, is illusory and fails the fallback element that the cap be based on 12 months of fees. The cap keys to "Fees", which § 1.5 defines as only "the Implementation Fee", and § 1.6 defines that as "the one-time implementation charge of USD 12,000 stated in the first Order Form". Because the charge is one-time and the cap is further confined to "the first Order Form", the twelve-month look-back captures nothing recurring: the cap is a fixed USD 12,000 ceiling, not 12 months' fees. Recurring spend plainly exists and is excluded — § 7.2 contemplates "annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance" and § 8.3 governs increases to "recurring Fees" — so the effective cap sits far below six months' fees, which is expressly walk-away territory. This also caps Vendor's exposure at USD 12,000 while Customer's payment obligations remain outside the cap under § 21.3, compounding the asymmetry in practice.

Because every other preferred element is already satisfied, I targeted the preferred level and made the single smallest change: one replace in § 21.1 substituting the narrow "Fees ... under the first Order Form" basis with all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months, and adding the USD 1,000,000 floor. I did not broaden the § 1.5 "Fees" definition itself, since that would also inflate Customer's liquidated-damages exposure under § 7.7; the fix is contained within the liability section. Mutuality, the damages exclusion and the carve-outs are preserved untouched.

proposal.summary: Fix the illusory cap quantum in § 21.1: cap becomes the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap set at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000. As drafted the cap keys to "Fees", which § 1.5 defines as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the cap is effectively USD 12,000 and sits far below six months' actual spend. We have referred to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and added the USD 1,000,000 floor; mutuality, the indirect-damages exclusion and the Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, which remain outside the cap) are unchanged.
